banner.headline: Taxonomic Lineage Explorer
banner.subcopy: Select any botanical family below to inspect diagnostic anatomical traits, evolutionary clade placement, and all documented species monographs belonging to that lineage.

Anacardiaceae.description: Resin-bearing tropical trees and shrubs known for compound or simple leathery foliage, panicle inflorescences, and aromatic drupes.
traits: Resin canals in bark yielding turpentine-scented oleoresins and phenolic mangiferin
Dense branched terminal panicles with tiny pentamerous nectary discs
Fleshy stone fruits (drupes) adapted for vertebrate dispersal

Rosaceae.description: Iconic flowering shrubs and temperate-to-subtropical ornamentals characterized by stipulate compound leaves, showy five-parted corollas, and numerous stamens.
traits: Perigynous hypanthium cup bearing spiralled or pentamerous petals
Alternate stipulate leaves often armed with epidermal prickles
High aromatic terpene ester synthesis in floral petals

Asteraceae.description: Earth's largest flowering plant family, distinguished by composite flower heads (capitula) uniting sterile ray florets and fertile central disc florets.
traits: Capitulum inflorescence mimicking a single giant blossom
Single-seeded achene fruits frequently topped with calyx pappus
Rich carotenoid pigments and heliotropic or aromatic terpenes

Apocynaceae.description: Milky-latex herbs, climbers, and tropical shrubs renowned for contorted five-lobed pinwheel corollas and pharmacologically active indole alkaloids.
traits: Opposite glossy simple leaves and milky or clear laticifer sap
Salverform tubular corollas twisting in bud (contorted aestivation)
Paired elongated follicle seed pods and vinca alkaloid chemistry

Rubiaceae.description: Tropical shrubs and trees marked by opposite simple leaves linked by interpetiolar stipules and dense corymb clusters of four-lobed tubular flowers.
traits: Strictly opposite leaves connected by triangular interpetiolar stipules
Hemispherical corymb inflorescences attracting butterflies & sunbirds
Fleshy berry-like drupes maturing from scarlet-orange blooms

Nymphaeaceae.description: Ancient aquatic rhizomatous herbs bridging early flowering plant evolution, anchored in wetland silt with floating peltate leaves and buoyant aerenchyma.
traits: Spongy gas-filled aerenchyma channels inside long flexible petioles
Floating orbicular pads with waxy water-shedding upper cuticles
Spiral transition between outer petals and inner pollen stamens

Moraceae.description: Laticiferous tropical canopy giants producing milky latex and remarkable multiple fruits—ranging from inverted fig syconia to cauliflorous jackfruit syncarps.
traits: Abundant white milky latex across bark, petioles, and fruit
Conical sheathing stipules leaving circular scars on twigs
Compound multiple fruits (syconia or trunk-borne syncarps)

Meliaceae.description: Drought-resilient timber and medicinal trees of the mahogany order featuring pinnately compound foliage and bitter insect-repellent limonoid triterpenoids.
traits: Imparipinnate drooping foliage with asymmetrical falcate leaflets
Staminal tube uniting filaments into a central floral column
Rich azadirachtin and limonoid phytochemistry in seeds and bark

Lamiaceae.description: Aromatic mint-family herbs and subshrubs distinguished by square cross-section stems, opposite decussate leaves, and glandular trichomes.
traits: Quadrangular (four-angled) stems and decussate aromatic leaves
Verticillaster whorled flower spikes attracting native bees
Essential oil glands rich in eugenol, camphor, and rosmarinic acid

Malvaceae.description: Mucilaginous mallow shrubs and trees famed for showy funnel blossoms bearing a prominent monadelphous staminal column fused around the style.
traits: Monadelphous stamens fused into an exserted crimson column
Epicalyx bracteoles beneath a five-lobed valvate calyx
Polysaccharide mucilage cells in petals, bark, and leaves

Oleaceae.description: Olive and jasmine woody climbers and trees recognized by opposite leaves and intensely fragrant, star-like white corollas rich in benzyl acetate.
traits: Opposite simple or trifoliate leaves without stipules
Nocturnal fragrance release timed for crepuscular moth pollination
Paired stamens attached inside slender tubular floral throats

Nelumbonaceae.description: Sacred emergent wetland lineage distinct from water lilies, possessing superhydrophobic aerial peltate leaves and flat-topped obconical seed receptacles.
traits: Self-cleaning micro-papillose wax leaf surfaces ('Lotus Effect')
Thermogenic blossoms regulating internal temperature for pollinators
Long-lived stony nutlets embedded in a spongy shower-head torus

Arecaceae.description: Unbranched woody monocot palms crowned with rosettes of giant pinnate fronds, ringed cylindrical trunks, and fibrous coastal drupes.
traits: Solitary cylindrical trunk lacking secondary cambial wood rings
Giant pinnate crown fronds protected by woven fibrous leaf bases
Liquid-to-solid endosperm nutrition inside buoyant husk drupes

Poaceae (Bambusoideae).description: Woody bamboo subfamily of the true grasses exhibiting hollow internodes separated by solid diaphragms, silica-armoured culms, and rapid elongation.
traits: Segmented hollow culms reinforced with biogenic silica and nodal rings
Interlocking pachymorph underground rhizomes stabilizing riverbanks
Fastest recorded daily shoot extension in terrestrial flora

Asphodelaceae.description: Arid-adapted succulent monocots storing mucilaginous acemannan water gel in thick basal leaf rosettes and utilizing nocturnal CAM photosynthesis.
traits: Basal rosettes of spiralled fleshy leaves with cartilaginous marginal teeth
Dual-layer leaf anatomy: clear inner gel parenchymal + bitter anthraquinone rind
Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) conserving desert moisture

Orchidaceae.description: Hyper-diverse epiphytic and terrestrial monocots featuring zygomorphic blossoms with a modified landing-platform petal (labellum) and spongy velamen roots.
traits: Bilateral symmetry with fused stamen-pistil column and labellum lip
Silvery spongy velamen root epidermis absorbing atmospheric mist
Symbiotic mycorrhizal dependence for microscopic dust-seed germination

Nyctaginaceae.description: Four-o'clock family climbers and thorny shrubs whose inconspicuous tubular flowers are framed by vivid papery petaloid bracts colored with betalains.
traits: Showy papery involucral bracts replacing petals in pollinator attraction
Betalain pigments (magenta, gold, coral) instead of anthocyanins
Curved woody stem spines enabling scrambling canopy ascent

Theaceae.description: Acidophilic evergreen montane shrubs and trees with finely serrated glossy foliage rich in caffeine alkaloids, L-theanine, and catechin polyphenols.
traits: Alternate leathery serrated leaves with translucent oil glands
Waxy five-petalled white blossoms filled with golden stamen clusters
Strong affinity for aluminum-rich, strongly acidic upland soils (pH 4.5–5.5)

Fabaceae.description: Cosmopolitan legume family ranging from herbaceous pulses to flamboyant umbrella canopy trees bearing compound pinnate leaves and elongated two-valved pods.
traits: Compound pinnate or doubly pinnate (bipinnate) feathery leaves with pulvinus joints
Distinctive five-petalled flowers featuring an ornate upper banner petal
Elongated dehiscent or woody seed pods (legumes) housing hard-coated seeds

Myrtaceae.description: Aromatic myrtle trees and shrubs distinguished by peeling mottled bark, opposite oil-gland foliage, and powder-puff blossoms bristling with hundreds of stamens.
traits: Exfoliating smooth copper-brown bark flaking in papery patches
Opposite leathery leaves dotted with fragrant terpenoid oil glands
Showy stamen-tufted blossoms yielding aromatic crowned berries and drupes

Sapindaceae.description: Subtropical soapberry trees producing pinnately compound foliage, terminal nectariferous panicles, and tuberculate fruits cradling juicy translucent edible arils.
traits: Evenly pinnate glossy foliage flushing coppery-salmon when young
Dense apetalous floral panicles featuring prominent honeybee nectary discs
Brittle pebbled pericarps enclosing a fleshy sweet aril around glossy seeds

Zingiberaceae.description: Aromatic tropical monocot herbs growing from fleshy horizontal rhizomes via clasping leafy pseudostems and shingled cone flower bracts rich in curcuminoids and volatile oils.
traits: Fleshy subterranean rhizomes concentrated with polyphenolic curcuminoids
Tubular overlapping leaf sheaths forming herbaceous upright pseudostems
Asymmetrical flowers tucked within colorful shingled cone-spike bracts

Solanaceae.description: Alkaloid- and steroidal-lactone-rich nightshades spanning culinary vegetables and dryland Ayurvedic subshrubs marked by bell-shaped corollas and fleshy berries.
traits: Radially symmetrical five-lobed bell or star corollas with connivent anthers
Accrescent papery bladder calyces enclosing orange berries in Physalis/Withania
Rich secondary metabolite synthesis (withanolides and alkaloids)

Pontederiaceae.description: Aquatic freshwater monocots equipped with spongy air-filled aerenchyma floats, feathery nutrient-scavenging roots, and tristylous lavender flower spikes.
traits: Inflated bulbous petioles packed with gas-filled honeycomb aerenchyma
Dense trailing violet root curtains absorbing aquatic nitrates rapidly
Orchid-like six-tepalled spikes bearing golden peacock-eye nectar guides
